# Practical Exercise: A Split Plot Experiment for Seafood Hygiene 

This exercise is useful for the following courses:

- 161.222;
- 228.371;
- and general revision on experimental design topics.

## Aims of this practical exercise


In this exercise you will:

- Analyse a simple split plot experiment with only two factors.

## Before you undertake this exercise...


## Storage of Seafood

Two types of seafood (mussels and oysters) were put in cool storage at three temperatures (0, 5, and 10 degrees). The response variable eing measured is the natural log of the bacteria count present on each item after two weeks in storage.

The constraint on this experiment was that only nine cool stoarage units were available. Both types of seafood could fit into each unit at the same time though, but rather obviously, each unit can only have one temperature. There are eighteen observations in all.


``` {r}
Seafood = read.csv("Seafood.csv") |>
mutate(across(c(Unit:Type), as.factor)) |>
glimpse()
```

## Required:

Use the `nlme` package to fit the appropriate model for this scenario. To do so means you must identify the random effect.

```{r}
Seafood.lme1 = lme(lnCount~Type*Temp, random=~1|Unit, Seafood)
Seafood.lme1 |> anova()
```
```{r}
Seafood.lme2 = lme(lnCount~Type+Temp, random=~1|Unit, Seafood)
Seafood.lme2 |> anova()
```

```{r}
plot(Seafood.lme2)
```

Interaction term has no positive effect on the model. The model without an interaction term has significant treatment variables. 



Investigate the residuals for your model. Is there anything to be concerned about?
No, the residuals seem to have equal variance. 

How will you depict/display the important differences among treatments for this experiment?


```{r}
Seafood.lme2 |> emmeans("Type")
```

```{r}
Seafood.lme2 |> emmeans("Temp") |> 
pairs(adjust = "tukey")  |> confint()
```

```{r}
plot(emmeans(Seafood.lme2, ~ Temp + Type), adjust = "tukey")

```

```{r}
SF_Type <- Seafood %>%
  group_by(Type, Temp) |>
  summarise(meanCount =mean(as.integer(lnCount)), .groups = 'drop')

Seafood %>% 
  ggplot(aes(y = lnCount, x = Temp, col = Type)) + geom_point() +
  geom_line(data= SF_Type, aes(y=meanCount, x = Temp, group = Type, col = Type))

```

Store seafood of oysters or mussels at lower temperatures. 0 is better than 5. Higher temperatures lead to higher bacteria counts.
